Gretchen Noelke, Intervenor, Pro Se Landowner, Opposing M7 and M22 Links​
SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26–16349​
PUC DOCKET NO. 59475


 JOINT APPLICATION OF ONCOR ELECTRIC                           §
 DELIVERY COMPANY LLC AND LCRA                                 §
 TRANSMISSION SERVICES                                         §        BEFORE THE
 CORPORATION TO AMEND THEIR                                    §
 CERTIFICATES OF CONVENIENCE AND                               §        STATE OFFICE OF
 NECESSITY FOR THE BELL COUNTY EAST                            §
 SWITCH TO BIG HILL SUBSTATION 765-KV                          §        ADMINISTRATIVE
 TRANSMISSION LINE PROJECT IN BELL,                            §
 BURNET, CONCHO, CORYELL, LAMPASAS,                            §        HEARINGS
 LLANO, MASON, MCCULLOCH, MENARD,                              §
 MILAM, MILLS, SAN SABA, SCHLEICHER, TOM                       §
 GREEN AND WILLIAMSON CRANES COUNTIES                          §



        INITIAL POST HEARING BRIEF OF INTERVENOR GRETCHEN NOELKE

COMES NOW, Gretchen Noelke, pro se, through her agent George Noelke, to submit her initial brief
pursuant to SOAH Order No. 6 in this cause.

  I.​    Introduction
    A.​ Gretchen Noelke is negatively impacted and thus opposes Links M7 and M22. The routes
         opposed by her are:​
         Routes 487, 494 and 499, all of which are in Link M7; and, ​
         Routes 547, 548, 295, 296 and 297, all of which are in Link M22.
    B.​ She filed a Statement of Position (Item 3994) and Direct Testimony (Item 3997) explaining that
         opposition in detail. Her discovery (Requests for Information) in this action was answered by
         Applicants (Item 5443).
    C.​ Gretchen Noelke participated in the Hearing on the Merits through her agent, George Noelke.
         She called no witnesses, and no party called her as a witness. Gretchen Noelke Exh. 1, her Direct
         Testimony, and Gretchen Noelke Exh. 2, Applicants’ responses to her Requests for Information,
         were both admitted as evidence by this Honorable Court.
    D.​ Applicants at the Hearing on the Merits failed to admit any evidence directly rebutting Gretchen
         Noelke’s claims as described in Statement of Position or Direct Testimony. On appeal of this
         matter, a contested case under the Texas Administrative Procedure Act, Applicants will lack the
         necessary substantial evidence required for them to locate their proposed 765 kV line on Gretchen


                                                                                                           1
            Noelke’s ranch. See PURA § 15.001 and Tex Gov’t Code § 2001.174.​


    II.​   Legal Argument
       A.​ Gretchen Noelke asserts that Applicants entirely failed to weigh the Texas Department of
           Agriculture’s (TDA) 2024 Family Land Heritage Program recognition of her ranch as having
           been in existence by the same family for more than 100 years. See Gretchen Noelke Exh. 1. ​
           1. This failure means that Applicants have improperly weighed the community, historical and
           aesthetic values1 related to her property. These should be weighed heavily in her favor such that
           Applicants’ proposed transmission line should not be located on her property. It is unreasonable
           for one state agency, the TDA, to recognize the historical value of her property, and another state
           agency, the PUC, to totally disregard that historical value.​
           2. Applicants blame TDA’s failure to adopt reliable data sets on the location of these recognized
           properties as the reason they did not consider this recognition. See RFI 1-06 in Gretchen Noelke
           Exh. 2. ​
           3. Notwithstanding the lack of data sets, Applicants conceded in cross during the Hearing on the
           Merits that it could consider ranches with this recognition as historical. See Transcript for June
           9, 2026 at pp 73-76. The Texas Department of Transportation, a state agency, considers these
           historical ranches when it considers routing, so it is unreasonable for Applicants to disregard
           them. Id. ​
           4. Therefore, Applicants failed to properly weigh Tracts 807, 808, 811, 812, 4423 and 4424. A
           CCN should not be granted that uses either M7 or M22 links.
       B.​ Calf Creek was also not evaluated in Applicants’ environmental analysis, and Applicants
           conceded in response to Gretchen Noelke’s discovery that flood prone areas were not ranked. See
           Gretchen Noelke Exh. 2 at RFI 1-05. ​
           1. Applicants’ failure to rank Calf Creek necessarily means that factors relating to community
           values, aesthetic values, costs, environmental integrity, engineering constraints and the policy of
           prudent avoidance have not been properly weighed as they relate to Gretchen Noelke’s property.2
           These should be weighed heavily in her favor such that Applicants’ proposed transmission line
           should not be located on her property. It is unreasonable for flood plain areas to go unranked,
           particularly on a property like hers that has received Family Land Heritage Program recognition.​
           2. Therefore, Applicants failed to properly weigh Tracts 807, 808, 811, 812, 4423 and 4424. A
           CCN should not be granted that uses either M7 or M22 links.
1
  The various factors are listed in PURA section 37.056(c) and 16 Texas Administrative Code section
25.101(b)(3)(B).
2
  Id. See PURA 37.056(c) and 16 Texas Administrative Code section 25.101(b)(3)(B).


                                                                                                                 2
     C.​ Gretchen Noelke asserts that, as applied, amended PURA §37.057 is not a grant of authority to
        the Applicants to disregard landowner Due Course of Law rights under the Texas Constitution,
        Tex. Const. art. I, § 19, Due Process rights under the U.S. Constitution, U.S. Const. Amend XIV,
        § 1 or those rights found in the Texas Administrative Procedure Act at Texas Gov’t Code §
        2001.051. The expedited 180 day calendar for these proceedings necessarily meant that she could
        not respond to or present evidence and argument on every issue in the case, as she is entitled
        pursuant to at Texas Gov’t Code § 2001.051. She is not arguing for a declaration that PURA
        §37.057 is unconstitutional, only that how it was applied in this proceeding (that has as many as
        700+ intervenors) is unconstitutional and deprived her rights under Texas Gov’t Code §
        2001.051.
    D.​ Finally, Gretchen Noelke supports the positions taken by the American Stewards of Liberty
        (ALS) on the deferral of the determination of need issues, as well as the Amici Curiae brief filed
        by certain Texas Legislators in this case. See Item 6139 for the Amici brief and a summary of the
        positions taken by ALS. She further supports the order abating the proceeding in 59029. See Item
        479 in 59029. In addition, great weight should be given to the testimony of PUC staff member
        Mr. Poole by Intervenor Ms. Graci. She asked him whether the load demand Applicants’ project
        should be re-evaluated since Google and others were currently developing gas-fired power
        generation projects for data centers.. He said in response, “...as the situation on the ground
        changes, then perhaps a re-evaluation is warranted. Transcript for Tuesday June 9, 2026 at p.
        289-290. Indeed, the situation on the ground is changing, and it is changing faster than
        Applicants can plow through these proceedings in 180 days.

III. Conclusion ​
Gretchen Noelke respectfully requests that this Honorable Court consider her arguments above when
drafting the Proposal for Decision.

Signed June 19, 2026

Respectfully submitted,​
​
​
/s/ Gretchen Noelke by agent George Noelke​
Gretchewn Noelke by agent George Noelke​
Intervenor​
Pro se landowner
